gradepilot.tagline: Making academic results easier to understand.
gradepilot.overview: GradePilot is a personal full-stack project designed to help students calculate and organize academic results. It started as a GPA and CGPA calculator inspired by the difficulty of working through university grading rules manually, and gradually evolved into an application with authentication, saved results, and academic insights.
challenges: Integrating Better Auth into the frontend and backend required significant debugging and a better understanding of authentication flows.
Translating academic grading rules into reliable calculation logic required careful research and iteration.
Keeping result-related interfaces understandable while introducing more features was an ongoing design consideration.
improvements: Explore adding academic schedules and routine-management features.
Improve calculation validation and edge-case handling.
Continue refining accessibility and the mobile experience.

zapshift.tagline: Exploring the systems behind parcel delivery.
zapshift.overview: ZapShift is a full-stack parcel delivery and logistics management project built as part of my web development learning journey. It explores how authentication, database operations, location-based interfaces, and delivery-related workflows can work together in a larger application.
challenges: Connecting frontend features with backend APIs and database operations.
Understanding how different user roles affect the application structure.
Working with location-based interfaces and delivery-related data.
improvements: Improve performance and usability across devices.

noxcodec.tagline: A terminal-inspired way to explore Morse code.
noxcodec.overview: NoxCodec is a frontend Morse code encoder and decoder inspired by my curiosity about Morse communication. The project combines a terminal-inspired visual style with interactive text conversion and audio feedback, making the experience both practical and enjoyable.
challenges: Handling Morse code conversion in both directions while keeping interactions intuitive.
Coordinating audio feedback with dot-and-dash sequences.
Balancing a terminal-inspired appearance with readability and usability.
improvements: Explore a messaging experience built around Morse code.
Improve keyboard accessibility and input feedback.

tuition-finder.tagline: Exploring a platform for finding tutors and tuition opportunities.
tuition-finder.overview: Tuition Finder began from a local client inquiry and evolved from an initially simple frontend concept toward a full-stack application. The requirements changed during development, and the project was not completed or delivered as a paid client engagement. It remains an unfinished learning project that helped me think more carefully about defining requirements and managing scope.
challenges: Adapting to changing requirements as the proposed scope expanded from frontend data to full-stack functionality.
Planning application structure before requirements were fully clarified.
Learning the importance of scope definition and clear communication in client-oriented work.
improvements: Clarify and finalize the intended feature set.
Complete and verify the main tuition discovery workflows.
Improve form validation, error handling, and responsive usability.
